content: Image/texture data (uint8 RGBA, fixed 0-255 range, quantization already baked in by the format) and float tensor data (arbitrary dynamic range, denormals/NaN/Inf possible, unbounded magnitude) require fundamentally different quantization strategies before hashing -- treating uint8 image bytes with the same decimal-rounding logic written for floats is a category error (there's nothing to round, only cross-hardware blending/rasterization noise of +-1 LSB per channel to tolerate), while treating float tensors like image bytes misses the need for relative (ULP/percentile-based) rather than absolute decimal-place tolerance across very different magnitudes.
